1. INTRODUCTION
The project is a web based School Management System developed as part of the
requirements for Web System Technologies with JavaScript
 The system focuses on providing Apex Institute of Technology (AIT) with a
digital platform for managing student records, attendance, grades,
enrollment, faculty information, administrative data, and school merchandise
inventory in one secure system.
 This system addresses the limitations of AIT current manual and paper-
based processes including slow record processing, lost documents, human
errors in computing grades or attendance, no longer data entry, and difficulty
tracking information as the student population grows. It is being developed
to replace manual workflows with an efficient, reliable, and organized
solution that speeds up daily operations, improves data accuracy, reduces
paperwork, and ensures information is secure and easily accessible.
 JavaScript is used to provide interactive functions such as dynamic form
validation during enrollment and grade entry, real-time data manipulation for
attendance tracking and grade computation, responsive user interaction
within dashboards and search tools, dynamic content updates without
reloading pages and role based interface adjustments ensuring a smooth
fast and user friendly experience for every type of user.

performance

decisions.

9. SYSTEM DESIGN
WebSystemTechnologieswithJavaScript—SystemDocumentation

The system supports two connected processes: submitting a request and tracking
its status. To submit a request, the user browses and optionally searches or filters the
Merchandise Catalog, selects an item, and is taken to the Request Form with the category
and item already filled in. After completing the remaining fields and clicking Submit, the
system validates the entry — displaying an error and returning the user to the form if any
required field is missing or invalid, or generating a unique Request ID and confirming
successful submission if all fields are valid. To track a request, the user enters this
Request ID and clicks Track Request. The system checks whether the ID exists; if not, it
shows a "request not found" message and prompts re-entry, and if found, it retrieves the
request data and displays the item, submission date, and current status on a progress
timeline that moves through four stages: Submitted, Processing, Preparing, and Ready for
Pickup.
Actor and Interactions
The system has a single actor: the AIT Student/Staff (Requester), representing any
member of the AIT community who accesses the merchandise system. This actor
interacts with the system in seven ways: browsing the merchandise catalog, searching or
filtering available items, submitting a merchandise request, tracking the status of a
submitted request, viewing the FAQ section, submitting a contact inquiry, and viewing the
Privacy Policy or Terms of Service. Since the system does not include a login or staff-
facing interface, all these interactions are available directly to the same actor without
requiring authentication.

AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Apex Institution of Technology (AIT) Online Merchandise Request and Tracking
System is a proposed web-based platform designed to improve access to the school's merchandise
information and make the merchandise request process more organized and convenient for
students and staff.
The system focuses on three current merchandise categories: School Uniform, PE Uniform,
and ID & Laces. Users can browse the merchandise catalog, search and filter available items,
create an account, log in, submit a merchandise request, and monitor the displayed progress of a
submitted request.
The proposed platform provides a single, organized interface for merchandise-related
activities. A request form collects the information needed to identify the requester and the selected
merchandise, while validation helps reduce incomplete or invalid submissions. A request tracking
feature provides a reference ID and displays the request through the stages Submitted, Processing,
Preparing, and Ready for Pickup.
For the current prototype, JavaScript provides the interactive behavior of the website, while
browser local storage is used to demonstrate account and request persistence without requiring a
backend database. This approach is suitable for demonstrating the intended workflow in an
academic prototype, but it is not intended to replace centralized, server-side storage and
production-grade authentication in a future deployment.
2. INTRODUCTION
Web technologies can help educational institutions make information and services more
accessible to their communities. A well-organized website can reduce the need to rely on separate
manual inquiries by placing frequently needed information and transactions in one accessible
platform.
Apex Institution of Technology (AIT) offers school merchandise that may be needed by
students and staff, including school uniforms, PE uniforms, and identification accessories. When
merchandise information and request procedures are handled through informal or manual methods,
AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System

users may have difficulty finding current product information, completing requests, or checking
the progress of their submissions.
The proposed AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System addresses this
concern by providing a dedicated web-based platform for browsing merchandise, submitting
requests, and tracking request status. The system also incorporates account registration and login
so that request information can be associated with the user during the prototype workflow.
The project demonstrates the practical use of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in creating an
interactive and responsive service-oriented website. It is intended to provide a clearer and more
convenient merchandise request experience while serving as a prototype that can be expanded in
future development.
3. BACKGROUND OF THE STUDY
School merchandise is part of the services that may be provided by educational institutions.
Students and staff may need uniforms and identification accessories for academic and institutional
activities. Access to clear and organized merchandise information can make it easier for users to
determine what is available and what information is required to submit a request.
Without a dedicated online platform, users may need to depend on manual inquiries or
separate communication channels to obtain merchandise information. This can make the request
process less organized and can make it difficult for users to monitor the status of a previous request.
The proposed system is intended to organize these activities through one web interface.
Instead of presenting merchandise information and request procedures separately, the website
combines product browsing, request submission, account access, and request tracking into a single
user flow.
The project is therefore centered on service accessibility and request organization rather
than on general academic record management. Features such as grades, attendance, enrollment,
teacher record management, and other school-wide administrative modules are outside the current
system proposal.
4. OBJECTIVES OF THE STUDY
AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System

4.1 General Objective
The primary objective of the project is to develop a web-based merchandise request and
tracking system for Apex Institution of Technology that provides an organized way for students
and staff to browse available school merchandise, submit requests online, and monitor the
displayed progress of their requests.
4.2 Specific Objectives
• To develop a responsive merchandise catalog that presents AIT's current School Uniform, PE
Uniform, and ID & Laces offerings in an organized manner.
• To provide search and category-filtering functions that help users locate merchandise more
conveniently.
• To implement user registration and login features for accessing account-related functions.
• To develop a merchandise request form that collects the necessary requester and item details
in a structured format.
• To apply JavaScript-based input validation to help prevent incomplete or invalid submissions.
• To generate unique request reference IDs for submitted merchandise requests.
• To implement a request tracking feature that displays request information and its current
prototype status.
• To associate submitted merchandise requests with the currently logged-in user within the
prototype environment.
• To provide a responsive and user-friendly interface that can be accessed through common
desktop and mobile web browsers.
• To demonstrate the use of browser local storage for persisting prototype account and request
data without a backend database.
5. SIGNIFICANCE OF THE STUDY
AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System

The proposed AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System is intended to make
merchandise information and request activities more organized and accessible. The project may
benefit the following groups:
5.1 For Students
• Convenient Merchandise Browsing – Students can view available merchandise categories and
product information through one online platform.
• Simplified Request Submission – Students can enter the required information through a
structured online request form.
• Request Tracking – Students can use their request reference ID and account-related features to
review the displayed progress of submitted requests.
• Accessible Information – Students can access merchandise information without relying
entirely on separate or manual inquiries.
5.2 For Faculty and Staff
• Convenient Access – Faculty and staff can browse available merchandise and submit requests
through the same platform.
• Organized Request Information – Standardized form fields help structure the information
provided by requesters.
• Improved Request Visibility – The tracking feature provides a clear way to review the
displayed stage of a request.
5.3 For the Institution
• Improved Service Accessibility – AIT can present its merchandise information and request
procedure through a dedicated digital platform.
• More Organized Request Workflow – A standardized request process can provide more
consistent collection of merchandise request information.
• Digital Service Development – The project demonstrates the use of web technology to support
an institutional service.
AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System

• Foundation for Future Development – The prototype can serve as a basis for later
improvements such as centralized data storage, staff-side request management, and stronger
authentication.
5.4 For Future Researchers and Developers
• Reference for Similar Projects – The project may serve as a reference for students developing
service-oriented web systems.
• Basis for Future Enhancement – Future developers can extend the prototype with backend
technologies, centralized databases, improved access control, and additional request-
management capabilities.
6. SCOPE AND LIMITATIONS
The proposed system is limited to AIT's online merchandise service. Its primary purpose
is to present available merchandise, allow eligible users to create accounts and log in, accept
merchandise requests, and provide a request-tracking interface.
6.1 Scope
• Merchandise Catalog – Displays the current merchandise categories: School Uniform, PE
Uniform, and ID & Laces.
• Search and Filtering – Allows users to search for merchandise and filter items by category.
• User Registration and Login – Allows users to create accounts and log in to account-related
features.
• Merchandise Request Form – Collects requester details, merchandise selection, size, quantity,
and additional notes.
• Request Validation – Checks required fields and basic input validity before submission.
• Request Reference ID – Generates a unique reference identifier for each submitted
merchandise request.
• Request Tracking – Displays the request item, submission information, and prototype status
timeline.
AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System

• Account Request History – Allows the logged-in user to view merchandise requests associated
with the account within the prototype.
• Responsive Web Interface – Supports access through common web browsers on desktop and
mobile-sized screens.
6.2 Limitations
• The system does not include academic records such as grades or attendance.
• The system does not include student enrollment, registrar processing, finance management, or
teacher management modules.
• The current prototype does not use a centralized backend database.
• Data stored through browser local storage is limited to the browser environment and is not
automatically synchronized across devices.
• The local-storage login mechanism is for prototype demonstration and is not equivalent to
production-grade server-side authentication.
• Request status stages demonstrate the intended workflow and should not be treated as a live
connection to a real merchandise fulfillment process unless such an integration is implemented.
• Online payment processing, delivery services, and dedicated native mobile applications are
outside the current scope.
7. PROPOSED SYSTEM FEATURES
Merchandise Catalog – Presents available AIT merchandise with product information and
organized categories.
Search and Category Filter – Allows users to search by merchandise name and filter items by
School Uniform, PE Uniform, or ID & Laces.
User Registration – Allows a user to create an account using the information required by the
prototype.
User Login and Logout – Allows registered users to access account-related functions and end the
active session.
AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System

My Account – Displays the logged-in user's basic account information and associated
merchandise requests.
Merchandise Request Form – Collects the user's personal information and selected merchandise
details for submission.
Dynamic Item Selection – Updates available merchandise choices according to the selected
category.
Form Validation – Uses JavaScript to check required fields and basic input validity before
submission.
Request Reference ID – Creates a unique identifier for a submitted merchandise request.
Request Tracking – Uses the request reference ID to retrieve and display request details and the
prototype status timeline.
Local Storage – Stores prototype account, session, and request data in the browser so the
workflow can persist after page refreshes.
8. CONCLUSION
The AIT Online Merchandise Request and Tracking System is proposed as a focused web-
based solution for improving access to school merchandise information and organizing the
merchandise request process of Apex Institution of Technology. By combining a merchandise
catalog, search and filtering, user accounts, request submission, and request tracking in one
interface, the system provides a more structured way for students and staff to interact with AIT's
merchandise service.
The current prototype demonstrates the intended workflow using JavaScript and browser
local storage. Its purpose is to demonstrate the system concept and core interactions within the
scope of an academic project. Future development may extend the prototype through a backend
system, centralized data storage, stronger authentication, staff-side management, and other
features required for real-world deployment.
